title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## SpatialHarness: Test-Time Spatial Scaffolding

### The Breakthrough
SpatialHarness adds virtual camera views at test time to improve spatial observability for fine manipulation. By keeping an online simulated replica and generating complementary virtual perspectives, it feeds a frozen GPT‑16 Astra policy, raising success from 26.7% to 66.7% on plug insertion and from 0% to 100% on a Tower of Hanoi task. The results highlight that many failures stem from missing visual cues rather than weak policies.

### The Caveats
The work benchmarks only the frozen GPT‑16 Astra policy and offers no comparison to alternative policies or stronger baselines, so the gains may not be solely due to the scaffolding.

## VersaCamVLA: Camera-Configurable VLA

### The Breakthrough
VersaCamVLA separates camera‑set representation from action learning, encoding any number of posed RGB images into a constant‑size latent scene token via multi‑signal target‑view prediction. Wrist‑Augmented Pose Sampling provides free diverse training poses, and the tokens are injected into a pretrained VLA as an extra visual condition, enabling policies that adapt to arbitrary camera configurations. The method outperforms existing VLA and multi‑view baselines on simulated benchmarks and a real‑robot testbed.

### The Caveats
The paper never ablates its central scene‑token encoder or the WAPS training trick, leaving the source of the reported gains unclear.

## Dex-One2Many: One-Demo Dexterous Manipulation

### The Breakthrough
The framework converts a single human video into sequential scene graphs that serve as reset‑state samplers and dense stage‑wise rewards, dramatically narrowing RL exploration. Graph‑based constraints focus on relational information, allowing policies trained entirely in simulation to transfer zero‑shot to a real multi‑fingered hand across five tool‑use tasks, with a 6.5% improvement in seen setups and up to 71% in unseen scenarios.

### The Caveats
Baseline methods are not named or described, so the reported gains cannot be verified against existing approaches.

## CSF: Contextual Safety Filtering

### The Breakthrough
CSF introduces a training‑free safety filter that grounds natural‑language safety rules in paired safe and unsafe reference trajectories, creating affine safety values enforced via a control‑barrier‑function QP. Demonstrated on a Unitree G1 robot, it cuts dangerous event rates by up to 90% while preserving 88‑100% of benign motions across four pretrained whole‑body motion generators.

### The Caveats
No baseline comparison to existing safety methods is provided, leaving the improvement unsubstantiated.

## rosnav: Full-Stack ROS2 Navigation Suite

### The Breakthrough
rosnav stitches Nav2, SLAM Toolbox, RTAB‑Map, ORB‑SLAM3 VSLAM, and an MPPI controller under a behavior‑tree framework, exposing a single launch that starts Gazebo Harmonic, SLAM, navigation, and RViz visualisation. It adds collaborative loop‑closure, coordinated frontier exploration for fleet‑level mapping, and a Gaussian‑Splatting overlay, with optional YOLO detection and LLM‑driven voice commands.

### The Caveats
Performance is never benchmarked against any baseline or quantitative metric; evaluation is confined to Gazebo simulations with no real‑world robot tests.

## SAGE: Persistent Identity Engine for Frozen LLMs

### The Breakthrough
SAGE wraps a frozen LLM with a metabolic‑state loop, salience‑gated attention, multi‑path memory, and identity/trust tensors, enabling agents that retain state across interactions. A fleet of eight heterogeneous machines runs 21 instances, logging over 2,700 developmental sessions, demonstrating scalable, persistent deployments.

### The Caveats
The repository provides no comparison to existing baselines, so it is unclear whether its scaffolding actually improves over standard frozen‑LLM approaches.

## Tessary: Open-Source AI Agent Failure Detection

### The Breakthrough
Tessary monitors every production AI‑agent trace with a two‑layer approach: cheap L1 classifiers flag suspicious traces at 2‑3 orders of magnitude lower cost, then state‑of‑the‑art L2 models diagnose root causes. On 1 M traces it achieves roughly a 5× cost reduction versus a sampled‑evaluation baseline.

### The Caveats
No comparison to other monitoring tools or latency/hardware overhead measurements is provided, leaving the claimed efficiency unverified.

### Priority
SpatialHarness shows how adding test‑time virtual views can instantly double or even fully eliminate failure rates in fine manipulation, making it the most actionable breakthrough today.

### One action
Integrate a test‑time virtual‑view generation module into your manipulation pipeline to boost spatial observability and success rates.
